description:
Here are the descriptions of the provided plots, following your guidelines:

The plots illustrate the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics. Both axes share a linear scale. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence”, ranges from 0.86 to 1.00 with increments of 0.01, and has no units. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy”, ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with increments of 0.2, and has no units. 

The first line, representing “Final Accuracy”, is blue with circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 0.73 at an initial confidence of 0.86, remains relatively stable around 0.92 between initial confidence values of 0.89 and 0.97, and then declines to approximately 0.86 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The second line, representing “Δ Accuracy”, is yellow with triangular markers and a solid line style. It starts at approximately 0.25 at an initial confidence of 0.86, decreases to approximately 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.93, and then increases to approximately 0.18 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The third line, representing “Initial Accuracy”, is green with square markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 0.78 at an initial confidence of 0.86, increases to approximately 0.86 at an initial confidence of 0.95, and then declines to approximately 0.81 at an initial confidence of 1.00.
